Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese garganta; from a substrate language *gʷr̥h₃gn̥t- (“throat”), cognate with Proto-Celtic *brāgants (“neck, throat”) and English craw (from Proto-Germanic *k(w)ragan(þ)-),[1] from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerh₃- (“to swallow”).[2][3] Alternatively, onomatopoeic.[4]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • IPA(key): /ɡaɾˈɡanta/ [ɡɑɾˈɣ̞ɑn̪.t̪ɐ]
  • IPA(key): (standard) /ɡaɾˈɡanta/ [ɡɑɾˈɣ̞ɑn̪.t̪ɐ]
  • IPA(key): (gheada) /ħaɾˈħanta/ [ħɑɾˈħɑn̪.t̪ɐ]

  • Rhymes: -anta
  • Hyphenation: gar‧gan‧ta

Noun

[edit]

garganta f (plural gargantas)

  1. (anatomy) throat
    Synonym: gorxa
  2. (anatomy) gullet
  3. gorge
    Synonym: desfiladeiro

Derived terms

[edit]
  • gargantada
  • gargantilla

Related terms

[edit]
  • gargal
  • gargallada
  • gargallo

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
garganta
Wikipedia pt

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese garganta; from a substrate language *gʷr̥h₃gn̥t- (“throat”), cognate with Proto-Celtic *brāgants (“neck, throat”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerh₃- (“to swallow”). Alternatively, onomatopoeic.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ɡaʁˈɡɐ̃.tɐ/ [ɡaɦˈɡɐ̃.tɐ]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ɡaʁˈɡɐ̃.tɐ/ [ɡaɦˈɡɐ̃.tɐ]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /ɡaɾˈɡɐ̃.tɐ/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ɡaʁˈɡɐ̃.tɐ/
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /ɡaɻˈɡɐ̃.tɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ɡaʁˈɡɐ̃.ta/ [ɡaɦˈɡɐ̃.ta]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ɡɐɾˈɡɐ̃.tɐ/ [ɡɐɾˈɣɐ̃.tɐ]

  • Audio (Brazil (Caipira)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɐ̃tɐ
  • Hyphenation: gar‧gan‧ta

Noun

[edit]

garganta f (plural gargantas)

  1. (anatomy) throat (posterior region of the oral cavity)
  2. (anatomy) throat (anterior-superior part of the neck)
  3. canyon, narrow (narrow passage between mountains)
  4. (figuratively) voice
  5. (figuratively) verbiage
  6. (figuratively) boast

Descendants

[edit]
  • Indo-Portuguese: garganta
  • → Ambonese Malay: gargantang
  • → Manado Malay: gargantang
  • → North Moluccan Malay: gargantang
  • → Papiamentu: garganta

[edit]
  • “garganta”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “garganta”, in Dicionário infopédia da Lingua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Porto: Porto Editora, 2003–2026
  • “garganta”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Spanish

[edit]
Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
garganta
Wikipedia es

Etymology

[edit]

From a substrate language *gʷr̥h₃gn̥t- (“throat”), cognate with Proto-Celtic *brāgants (“neck, throat”) and English craw (from Proto-Germanic *k(w)ragan(þ)-),[1] from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerh₃- (“to swallow”).[2][3] Alternatively, onomatopoeic.[4] Compare English gargle.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɡaɾˈɡanta/ [ɡaɾˈɣ̞ãn̪.t̪a]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -anta
  • Syllabification: gar‧gan‧ta

Noun

[edit]

garganta f (plural gargantas)

  1. (anatomy) throat
  2. (geography) gorge
    Synonym: desfiladero

Hypernyms

[edit]
  • cuello m

Hyponyms

[edit]
  • esófago m
  • laringe f
  • tráquea f

Derived terms

[edit]
  • garganta profunda
  • nudo en la garganta

Descendants

[edit]
  • French: Gargantua (a character from François Rabelais's 16th-century pentalogy The Life of Gargantua and of Pantagruel.)
    • English: gargantuan
    • French: gargantuesque
  • → Haitian Creole: gagann

[edit]

  2. ^ Matasović, Ranko (2009), Etymological Dictionary of Proto-Celtic (Leiden Indo-European Etymological Dictionary Series; 9), Leiden: Brill, →ISBN, pages 72-73

  4. ^ Coromines, Joan; Pascual, José Antonio (1983–1991), “garganta”, in Diccionario crítico etimológico castellano e hispánico [Critical Castilian and Hispanic etymological dictionary]‎[2] (in Spanish), Madrid: Gredos
